items.title: Abbey Lincoln — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: His wife told me -- she came with me to the hotel and put my foot in a pail of hot water and epsom salts and cried and told me that she was sorry, but that he was -- he had been in the Army and he was shell shocked

ctx.x: You know, when you tell the story about this piano player, -­

His wife told me -- she came with me to the hotel and put my foot in a pail of hot water and epsom salts and cried and told me that she was sorry, but that he was -- he had been in the Army and he was shell shocked and that he carried a gun and that I shouldn't say anything to upset him. I told her he wasn't my husband, he was hers.

Still, I called the agent and I told him that I was going to sue him, but he didn't have any money, and I couldn't afford a doctor and so I went every night on his arm into the club and finished my work. Mm-hmm. And the club owner said that if I left, everybody would have to leave. So, I was really doing good even then, you know. Mm-hmm. I was the one. Anna Marie. I have some pictures of myself and also some of the -- a couple of marquees. Well, not really marquees, but, you know, advertising. The lovely Anna…
